You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

1. Your action is read only from the plain text of your reply, never from Python output or a tool call: printing JSON in Python or calling a tool named submit/request_demos/finish/answer does nothing. Keep each turn to a few tool calls, then reply in text ending with exactly one of {"action": "request_demos"}, {"action": "submit", "grid": [[ints]]}, {"action": "finish"} on the last line. Replies without a valid action waste the turn, and a few in a row end the puzzle charged in full.
2. When a message says "Decide now" or "could not find a valid action", make no tool call: reply at once in text with the action line. Submit only a grid already printed above (copy it); otherwise send {"action": "request_demos"}. You have not submitted anything until you see a verdict message.
3. With no demo pair yet, request_demos first: the test input alone cannot show the rule, so never submit before seeing a demo.
4. Never retype grids. Load every grid shown so far (rerun after each new demo):
```
import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])   # this instance's own log: the folder keeps every earlier one's
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
```
5. Write the rule as a Python function f and check f(demo input) == demo output for every demo pair. Submit only when all match, pasting the printed json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])). If one mismatches, fix f or request another demo; never resubmit a grid already judged wrong.
6. Once f matches every demo, submit instead of requesting more demos.

Rule: find rectangular regions of a distinct color, fill them solid with that color, replace stray pixels with background (3). In test, background is 6, blocks are 5-rectangle (rows 5-10, cols 6-11) and 8-block (rows 3-4, cols 15-21). Noise: 4s scattered.

Note in demo, the 1-block: corrupted pixels inside replaced by 1; also pixels adjacent? The 4 at (5,13),(5,16)? In output they became 3. Noise 5 at (12,17)→3. Also 7 at (6,3),(6,6)→3.

So f: for each non-background color forming a rectangle shape, fill its bounding box with that color; all other non-background pixels → background. Need to detect blocks vs noise. In test: color 5 forms rectangle rows 5-10 cols 6-11 (with noise 4s inside); color 8 forms rows 3-4 cols 15-21 rectangle (with 4 inside). Background 6.

But careful: in demo, background is 3, blocks are 0 and 1. Noise colors are various (5,7,8,6,4). Noise doesn't form rectangles.

Implementation: background = most common color. For each other color c, get cells; if they form "mostly rectangle" — bounding box where cells occupy most positions? Fill bounding box with c. But some noise colors are isolated single pixels — bounding box 1x1 fill = the pixel itself, which would keep noise! Need to distinguish blocks from noise. In demo, noise pixels are single pixels of colors like 5,7,8,4,6 — same colors possibly as blocks? Block colors are 0 and 1. Noise includes 5,7,8,6,4 — distinct from block colors here. Hmm, but in test noise color 4, blocks 5 and 8 — distinct. Simple heuristic: fill bounding box for colors whose cell count within bounding box ≥ some fraction (e.g., ≥70%)? Check demo: 0-block 6x5=30 cells, all 0s except... rows0-5 cols3-7 all 0 — yes 30 cells. 1-block rows14-17 cols3-9: 4x7=28 cells, one cell is 7, rest 1 → 27/28. Noise singletons: 1 cell/1 → 100%. Problem: singletons pass. Distinguish by size: blocks are larger, e.g., ≥ 2 rows and 2 cols. Noise pixels are single. Check demo noise: all noise are isolated single pixels? 5 at (0,11),(0,17),(1,0)... singles. Seems yes.

But also noise could be same color as a block adjacent? Ignore.

Alternative approach: rectangle detection: a set of cells of color c that contains at least one maximal run... Simpler: for color c, compute bounding box; if cells ≥ 4 (or height≥2 and width≥2) and density high, fill. Singleton noise: bbox 1x1 → not filled → set to background.

Check demo: any noise pixel adjacent to a block extending bbox? 0-block bbox cols3-7 rows0-5; noise 7 at (1,3)? Row1: "5 3 3 7 0 0 0 0..." col3 is 7! That's inside the block, not extending bbox. 6 at (2,6) inside block. 8 at (4,1)? outside. Fine.

1-block rows14-17 cols3-9: cell (14,3)=1... row14: "3 3 4 1 1 1 1 4 1 1 7..." cols3-9: 1,1,1,1,4,1,1 — 4s inside. Row16: "1 1 8 1..." col3=1, col8=8? row16: "3 3 3 1 1 1 1 1 8 1" col8=8 inside. bbox rows14-17 cols3-9: 28 cells, 24 ones. Density fine.

But careful: noise pixel of same color as a block elsewhere could enlarge bbox. E.g., test color 8: block rows3-4 cols15-21; any other 8s? Looking at test input, 8 appears only in that block. Color 5 only in block. Good.

Also demo: color 5 noise at multiple places, no 5-block. Color 8,7,6,4 noise only. Color 1: block plus... any stray 1? Row1 col12=1, inside 1-block? No, that's row1 col12 — far from block. Row 1: "5 3 3 7 0 0 0 0 6 3 3 3 1 5 1 1 1 1" — cols12,14-17 are 1! That's a partial row of the 1-block? No wait, output row1: "3 3 3 3 1 1 1 1 1 1" — cols12-17 all 1. So in input row1, 1s at 12,14,15,16,17 with 5 at 13. So the 1-block spans rows1-5 cols12-17! Input rows1-5 cols12-17 mostly 1 with noise. And block rows14-17 cols3-9 also 1. Two separate 1-blocks. And output fills both. Good — bounding box per color would merge them badly! So need connected components, not global bbox per color.

So: connected components of non-background cells; if a component is rectangle-ish (density high, size≥2x2 area... ), fill its bbox; else remove. Component (1,13) 5 is singleton removed. In row1, 1s at 12,14..17 — connected horizontally except gap at 13. Connectivity 8-way? 1 at (1,12) and (1,14) not adjacent. With 8-connectivity also not. So components: {12}, {14..17} plus connections down column: (2,12)=1, (3,12)=1... and (2,13)=1. So component includes (1,14..17) connected to (2,13..17) etc. And (1,12) connected to (2,12) diagonally/vertically: (2,12)=1 yes vertical. So all one component rows1-5 cols12-17: cells: row1: 12,14,15,16,17 (13 is 5); rows2-5: full. Count = 29/30. Good, one component, fill bbox rows1-5 cols12-17.

Careful: component of 1-block doesn't connect to 1s in rows14-17 — separated. Good.

But noise 4s inside blocks are separate components (singletons) — removed. But wait, when we fill the block bbox, does a noise pixel inside the bbox get overwritten? Order: fill rectangle, then remove non-rectangle components. Fill overwrites noise inside. Fine.

Also noise singleton touching block? e.g., 7 at (6,3) — row6 all 3s in output; input row6 "3 3 3 7 3 3 7 3..." these 7s are below 0-block, separate. Fine.

Edge risk: noise pixel diagonally connecting? Whatever.

Test: components: 5-block rows5-10 cols6-11 (with a 4 at (8,7)? row8: "6 6 6 6 6 6 5 4 5 5 5 5 4" — 4 at col7 and col12. col12 outside bbox (cols6-11). col7 inside). Fill rows5-10 cols6-11 with 5. 8-block rows3-4 cols15-21, with 4 at (3,16). Fill. Remove all 4s.
